decision_conditions: All tree works will be carried out in accordance with British Standard 3998: 2010 Tree work. Recommendations. In order to carry out the tree works to BS 3998:2010 there will be only the removal of secondary and tertiary branches, no primary branches. All finalpruning cuts on the branches will not exceed a third of the diameter of the main stem of the tree when measured at 1.5 meters above ground level. Reason: To ensure that the works are carried out in accordance with good arboricultural practice.

This decision notice for Tree Works is only valid for 2 years from the date of this decision or until the work is completed, whichever is the sooner. Reason: In order to ensure that the work is carried out whilst still appropriate and in accordance with the time period within the legislation and regulations.

A replacement tree for T1 shall be planted in accordance with the following specifications: Tree Species: Rowan, Holly, Hornbeam or BirchQuantity: x1 Size/Height: 10-12cm stem circumference at 1mTo be planted in accordance with the recommendations in British Standard 8545:  Trees from nursery to independence in the landscape - Recommendations (2014). Root ball or container grown is acceptable.Location: In the same position as the original tree, or in an alternative position to be agreed in writing by the Council.Deadline: Within 60  days following the removal of the original tree, or an alternative date to be agreed in writing by the Council.The tree shall thereafter be maintained and shall not be pruned or removed without the written consent of the Council.

The proposal to remove Ash tree T1 can be justified based on the tree's poor physiological condition and limited amenity value, resulting from past pollarding. A replacement tree is required to  renew the landscape feature, to ensure the value of the TPO is maintained. In relation to  T2 Holm Oak,  whilst the supporting evidence does identify that decay is present within the stem, the Council do  not consider that it is a proportionate response, at this stage,  to remove the tree entirely. This is where there are alternative and viable arboricultural options that can utilised manage risk and enable the Holm Oak to continue to make an important contribution to public visual amenity and toward  the character and appearance of the area.Lesser works have been granted to enable crown reduction works for T2 Holm Oak
